answer: Chorus-Latency Admission Gate. Each agent identity must sustain a genuinely irregular request cadence, measured as timing jitter with a quartz-stable reference clock. Traffic that is too smooth or too bursty fails the signal test and gets throttled. Real agents pass by exhibiting human-like variance in their traffic reef. To fake this at scale, an attacker must spend compute maintaining independent per-identity timing profiles, raising the marginal cost of each plausible identity well above its expected reward.
